Set parameter net.ipv4.tcp_timestamps to 0'; 'To prevent saptune from changing the manually set net.ipv4.tcp_timestamps value from 0 back to 1, update saptune version to 3.1.1 or higher'; the azure-lb resource answers port 625<instance no.> in a group colocated with the promoted HANA. brief.situation: You are the SAP Basis on call at Tarrow Chemicals. Production HANA (HN1, instance 03) runs in a SUSE Pacemaker cluster behind an internal Standard Load Balancer whose frontend 10.20.1.50 is the database's virtual IP. Last night's OS patching updated both HANA nodes. Since 06:10 every application server reports it cannot connect to 10.20.1.50; the cluster says HANA is running on hana-db1. Users start at 08:00.
handover: The patch run used the image's saptune version, 3.0.2.
The load balancer probes TCP 62503, answered by the cluster's azure-lb resource on the node that holds the primary.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the load balancer's frontend, its health probe and the two HANA nodes.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the virtual IP was unreachable with HANA up, what you changed, and how it is prevented.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Separates the load balancer's view from the cluster's.
parts.modelAnswer: The cluster showed HANA primary on hana-db1 with the probe listener running, but the load balancer saw no healthy backend since 06:08. The patch run's saptune 3.0.2 had set net.ipv4.tcp_timestamps back to 1, and with timestamps on Azure's health probes fail.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Fixes the setting, not the cluster.
parts.modelAnswer: Set net.ipv4.tcp_timestamps=0 on both nodes, persisted in /etc/sysctl.d; the probe went healthy and the application servers connected. A takeover would have moved HANA to a node with the same problem.

parts.label: Prevent
parts.criteria: Removes the cause and watches the symptom.
parts.modelAnswer: saptune is now 3.1.2 (which keeps the manual value) and in the patch baseline, and an alert fires on the load balancer's probe status.

expertPath.text: Cluster healthy; probe metric 0 since 06:08; tcp_timestamps 1 after the saptune 3.0.2 patch run; listeners up.
tcp_timestamps 0 on both nodes, persisted; saptune 3.1.2; alert on the probe metric.

needlessTakeover.headline: The cluster was not the problem
needlessTakeover.body: HANA and its probe listener were healthy; the load balancer's probes were failing at the kernel. A failover moves a healthy database onto a node with the same setting.

plantDown.headline: No healthy probe, no virtual IP
plantDown.body: An internal load balancer forwards to the virtual IP only while a backend answers its health probe. With TCP timestamps on, Azure's probes fail; set net.ipv4.tcp_timestamps to 0.

probing.headline: Good: the probe, not the cluster
probing.body: You saw the cluster was healthy and the load balancer was not, found the patch-reset kernel setting, fixed it without a failover, checked a real connection, and removed the cause.

gaps.headline: Held, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the evidence before the change, the lasting step, the check, or the cause in the record.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The cluster is healthy and the probe listener runs on the primary, yet the load balancer sees no healthy backend: the probes are failing. The patch run's saptune set TCP timestamps back on, and with timestamps on Azure's health probes fail. Set them off on both nodes and persist it; no failover is needed. Then update saptune so patching cannot undo it, and alert on the probe metric.
